static_traits.name: Li Na
static_traits.social_status: Relationship with spouse strained due to the negative mindset; has one close friend but has not yet shared feelings of failure and pessimism
static_traits.medical_history: No similar history of psychological problems; not yet received psychotherapy; no significant physical illness
static_traits.language_features: Neutral attitude; expresses clearly, can describe experiences and thoughts specifically; willing to cooperate in counseling (agreed to keep a journal)

basic_info.main_problem: I experienced a sense of failure and pessimism during the fishing trip; these feelings began with the most recent unsuccessful fishing experience.
basic_info.core_demands: Because the sense of failure and pessimism began to affect overall mood and enjoyment of the activity, seeking counseling to improve these feelings.
growth_experiences: One particularly awful fishing trip: the client expected to catch sunfish, but after trying different spots and techniques for hours still had not caught any fish. This setback significantly increased the sense of failure and pessimism; since then, every planned fishing trip brings fear of failing again, and the enjoyment of the activity has markedly declined.

A very successful fishing experience: last summer, the client caught many kinds of fish, felt pride and accomplishment, was more relaxed and confident in mindset, and focused on enjoying the process rather than the outcome.

special_situations.event: In the most recent fishing trip, expecting to catch sunfish but still having no catch after trying different spots and techniques for hours
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I have not reached the anticipated goal, it means I am not good enough -- terrible
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Continuously switching fishing spots and techniques during the same trip to prove oneself capable
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will probably fail next time too; I may never catch a fish again

special_situations.event: Every time planning the next fishing trip
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I fail again, it means I am not suited for this job, and my self-worth will be negated
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Reduces sharing inner feelings with others (friends), bearing it alone to avoid being evaluated
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will fail again; I am not worthy of being a fisher

special_situations.event: When reviewing past fishing experiences, recent failures overshadow past successes
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Only continued, recent success counts; past success does not mean I am capable
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Focusing on and repeatedly thinking about failure, belittling or ignoring evidence of success

core_conflict.wish: Longing to confirm self-worth and competence through success in fishing
core_conflict.fear: Fearing that failure will prove oneself not good enough, with identity and self-worth threatened
defense_goal: Lowering the impact of disappointment through pessimism and anticipating failure in advance
Avoids expressing feelings to others to avoid being judged

object_relations.self_representation: A failed practitioner who is not good enough
object_relations.object_representation: Spouse and children are the intimate others affected by my negative emotions

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When recalling the recent failed fishing experience or planning the next trip
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Equating one failure with overall incompetence, and believing the future is bound to bring failure (tightly binding self-worth to performance)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: In an empathic rather than judgmental tone, point out the tendency to negate past successes, inviting the identification and integration of success evidence; use open-ended questioning to guide distinguishing one failure from overall ability.

manifestations: Strongly binds fishing success to self-worth; a single failure prompts questioning 'who am I / am I valuable'
Enjoyment of activities decreases, other life interests also weaken

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact
manifestations: Repeated self-blame: 'I am not good enough / I am terrible'
Defining oneself and the future by one failure
Excessive worry before planned outings, anticipating failure

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the impulse originally wanting to express outward or seek others' help, and turns it on themselves instead; corresponds to 'impulse'
manifestations: Staying in touch with friends yet not sharing feelings of failure and pessimism
More irritable and withdrawn at home, digesting negative emotions inwardly rather than seeking support

exception_events.target_problem: In fishing activities, the client usually develops fear of failure and pessimism when planning or engaging, and thus reduces enjoyment of the activity
exception_events.unique_outcome: On a fishing trip last summer, the client caught many kinds of fish, with a more relaxed and confident mindset, focusing on enjoying the process, and experiencing pride and a sense of achievement
exception_events.reason: Different mindset and approach: more relaxed and confident at the time, focusing on the process itself rather than the outcome, so catastrophic prediction and excessive worry had not yet appeared

positive_force: Has many successful fishing experiences and an ability foundation (has had many good fishing trips)
Willing to try strategy adjustments (has changed fishing spots and techniques)
Has social support resources (one close friend to communicate with)
negative_force: Catastrophizing and black-and-white thinking patterns, tending to predict the future as failure
Negating positive experiences; past successes 'do not count'
Overly binding self-worth to performance; failure means self-denial
Avoiding expression and help-seeking, bearing pressure alone

target_behavior.behavior: When planning or going fishing, strong fear of failure and pessimistic predictions arise
antecedent: Recalling the most recent failed fishing trip
Facing fishing tasks and performance expectations at work
target_behavior.core_reason: One failure was overgeneralized and used to define self-ability, tightly binding self-worth to fishing success or failure, forming the cognitive chain of 'predicting the future' and 'black-and-white'
target_behavior.function: Avoids the strong negative feelings and damaged self-worth from potential failure
target_behavior.consequence: Decreased enjoyment of fishing and other activities, impaired work performance, overall low mood

target_behavior.behavior: Showing irritability and withdrawal in family interactions
antecedent: Low mood before and after planning or going fishing
Persistent negative mindset after recent failure experiences
target_behavior.core_reason: Influenced by feelings of failure and pessimistic cognitions and emotions, brings stress into family interactions
target_behavior.function: Avoiding exposure to and facing the self-perceived 'not good enough' and sense of failure by reducing contact with others
target_behavior.consequence: Relationship tension with spouse, interactions with children affected
